name: Mythic M1108
memory_bandwidth_basis: Not published. Mythic's analog architecture uses Flash memory cells for both storage and compute, so there is no separate memory bandwidth figure.

flops.notes: 35 TOPS INT8 (vendor claim). Some sources cite 45 TOPS; the lower figure is used as the more conservative number. The compute is analog in-memory, not digital tensor cores.

notes: REAL VENDOR: Mythic (mythic.ai). Set to 'asic-other' because the schema enum does not include 'mythic'. The M1108 is Mythic's first production analog compute-in-memory AI accelerator. It uses Flash memory cells for both storage and compute, eliminating the memory wall by performing matrix operations directly in the memory array. 35 TOPS INT8 at 4W. Supports ResNet-50 and YOLOv3 without external DRAM. Currently sampling; Mythic has raised $125M in funding (Dec 2025) to scale production. Target markets: automotive, defense, robotics, enterprise edge. NOT a datacenter LLM serving chip — the analog architecture is optimized for vision workloads at very low power. The company claims 100x energy efficiency vs GPUs but this is not independently verified. Mythic has pivoted from datacenter to edge focus. DANGLING REF, LEFT UNRESOLVED (2026-10-04 cross-reference repair): interconnect holds 'pcie', which is not a record id. The repo's interconnect records are generation-scoped - pcie-gen3, pcie-gen4, pcie-gen5, pcie-gen6 - and this record states no PCIe generation for the module anywhere; it only records form_factors ['m2'] and describes the part as an M.2 module. Picking a generation would be a guess, so the value was left unchanged.
